title: What are your labels?
html:
Good morning,

Some kids really are shy.

That's just how they're wired, right?

That's what I thought too... for a while.

My son would go quiet at family gatherings. Someone would lean down and say hi, and he'd look at the floor. Every time, someone nearby would whisper it.

"He's just shy."

And I felt the pull to agree. It's easier. Less awkward than saying anything back.

But here's the thing. The label bothered me. Because once he knew someone, he was fine. He'd talk nonstop. He'd laugh. He'd follow them around the house. That's not shyness. That's just a kid who hadn't warmed up yet.

So one Christmas, when my aunt said it again, I didn't let it go.

I said no. He's being rude. He needs to use his manners.

Right there, I got him to walk over, shake her hand, and look her in the eye.

He did it.

Is that really what a shy kid looks like?

There's a theory called labeling theory. The idea is simple. Call someone something enough times and they start to become it. Not because they were born that way. Because they believe the story.

"Shy" becomes their excuse. Then their identity. Then their ceiling.

He shakes hands easily now. Looks people in the eye. Doesn't think twice about it.

The label never stuck.

And that matters more than the manners.

To your success!

Glenn
